label: prf:q-exponential-exists
title: Proof of existence of the $q$-exponential grouplike
html:
Over R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]\bigl[\tfrac{1}{[n]_q!} : n \ge 1\bigr] the element

  \exp_q \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!} \;\in\; \mathcal{H}_q

is grouplike (via the q-binomial identity \Delta_q(x^n) = \sum_{k} \binom{n}{k}_q x^k \otimes x^{n-k}) and flow-invariant (via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q x^{n-1}, which shifts the series by one index while preserving the sum). Over \mathbb{C}, the non-root-of-unity condition q \notin \mu_\infty (existence of substrate parameter, Step 3) keeps each [n]_q! \ne 0, and the resulting series converges to the analytic q-exponential (the Taylor series of \exp_q, derived in the information-theory chapter). Over \mathbb{F}_p the hypothesis fails (the finite-field obstruction, remarked below); a truncated existence result holds modulo x^p = 0. Over \mathbb{Q}_p and \mathbb{C}_p existence follows from the Witt-vector lift (the p-adic \exp_q, remarked below).
